original_question: Does there exist a measure-preserving automorphism T of a probability space (X, B, mu) that is mixing but fails to be mixing of some higher order? Here T is k-fold mixing if for every measurable sets A, A_1, ..., A_k and every m_1, ..., m_k -> +infinity one has mu(A intersect T^{m_1}A_1 intersect T^{m_1+m_2}A_2 intersect ... intersect T^{m_1+...+m_k}A_k) -> mu(A)mu(A_1)...mu(A_k), and the paper denotes the class of such automorphisms by Mix(k).
target_in_paper: §1, Q1, the paper’s statement of Rokhlin’s multiple-mixing problem, immediately after the definition of k-fold mixing and the notation Mix(k).
correct_elements: Your draft correctly targets the main open problem stated in §1/Q1, namely whether ordinary mixing can fail to imply some higher-order mixing. It also correctly uses a measure-preserving automorphism of a probability space, correctly encodes k-fold mixing through higher-order correlation limits, and correctly records the paper’s notation Mix(k) for the class of k-fold mixing automorphisms.
missing_details: State explicitly that the question is existential over some integer k ≥ 2; the paper does not fix a particular higher order in advance.
Make explicit that ordinary mixing is the k = 1 case of the same definition.
Clarify that the limit is taken along sequences of integer time shifts m_1(n), ..., m_k(n) with m_i(n) → +∞ for each i.
Use a fully stand-alone indexing of measurable sets, e.g. A_0, ..., A_k, rather than mixing the roles of A and A_1, ..., A_k.
Say that this is Rokhlin’s problem for a single measure-preserving automorphism of a probability space, not the nearby Zd-action variant mentioned only as contrast.
If Mix(k) is mentioned, clarify that it is just the paper’s notation for the class of k-fold mixing automorphisms, not an extra hypothesis.
Avoid narrowing the problem to Mix(2) versus Mix(3) or to any spectral/joining/local-rank variant; those appear only as surrounding context in the paper.
refined_question: Rokhlin’s multiple-mixing problem for a single automorphism: does there exist a measure-preserving automorphism T of a probability space (X, B, μ) that is mixing (that is, 1-fold mixing) but is not k-fold mixing for some integer k ≥ 2? Here T is k-fold mixing if for every measurable sets A_0, ..., A_k in B and every sequences of integers m_1(n), ..., m_k(n) with m_i(n) → +∞ for each i, one has μ(A_0 ∩ T^{m_1(n)}A_1 ∩ T^{m_1(n)+m_2(n)}A_2 ∩ ... ∩ T^{m_1(n)+...+m_k(n)}A_k) → ∏_{j=0}^k μ(A_j). In the paper’s notation: is there a mixing automorphism that fails to belong to Mix(k) for some higher k?
justification: The exact official formulation matching your draft is §1, Q1. The paper introduces the definition of k-fold mixing and the notation Mix(k) immediately before Q1, so your draft is aimed at the right statement. The nearby §1 results, Theorems 1.1–1.3, are the paper’s main surrounding partial results about positive local rank, light 2-fold mixing, and quantitative deviations from multiple mixing, but they do not replace Q1. §2 then explains, through joinings, one mechanism that can force higher-order mixing, which confirms that Q1 itself—not a broader spectral, local-rank, or MSJ reformulation—is the narrow paper-faithful target.
